text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said Russian officials assured him that Moscow will repay all of the remaining $110 million of its debt to Slovakia inherited from the former Soviet Union. Russia has so far paid back some $50 million, mainly with deliveries of various goods.

- The Slovak government on Tuesday rejected a decision by the Confederation of Trade Unions (KOZ) to stop talks on a general agreement for this year for a government plan to regulate salary increases.

- The average nominal wage in the industrial sector in the first five months of the year rose 11.9 percent year-on-year. Wages in the construction sector increased by 15.7 percent while transport salaries rose by 12.5 percent.

- The National Property Fund (NPF) on Tuesday transferred a majority stake in chemical company Novacke Chemicke Zavody a.s. (NCHZ) to the little-known company PT Nova for 240 crowns per share despite a High Court ruling that Czech firm Inekon had the right to get a 51 percent in NCHZ as agreed with the NPF in 1994 when Inekon bought the stake for 1,500 crowns per a share.

SME - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said "many contries" did not use objective criteria for evaluating Slovakia which influenced the decision to exclude Bratislava from the first wave of NATO eastward enlargement.
- Opposition parties consider exclusion of Slovakia from NATO enlargement as a failure of the ruling coalition in pursuing Slovakia's strategic interests.

- Some 26.1 percent of Slovaks would vote for the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) if general elections were held last weekend. Opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) and the Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) would finish second, both getting some 13.4 percent.

- The ruling coaliton of Meciar's HZDS, the ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS) and the left-wing Workers Party (SDL) would get some 35.3 percent if elections were held last weekend, while a newly-created opposition coalition would get 31.3 percent of votes.
- Several Slovak rivers, mainly in the north-western part of the country, have over the past few days reached their highest water levels in the last 100 years.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The eight largest money market players on Tuesday failed to agree upon s resumption of the obligation to quote both offers and bids on interbank money market rates.
